record.original_question: For a fixed pattern x, consider the deterministic finite automaton suggested as a way to augment the Boyer-Moore string-search procedure so that it remembers which comparisons need not be repeated after a mismatch and shift. What is the exact number of states required by such a "Boyer-Moore dfa", or at least what are close upper and lower bounds on that state count as a function of the pattern?

evidence.quote: Question 2: The number of states in a "Boyer-Moore dfa". ... The question is to find the exact number, or alternatively close upper and lower bounds on the number of states such a dfa must have.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Fix a finite alphabet $\Sigma$ and a pattern $x = x_1 x_2 \cdots x_m \in \Sigma^m$. Recall the Boyer–Moore string-matching procedure: when searching for $x$ inside a text $t \in \Sigma^*$, the pattern is aligned with a window of the text and characters are compared from right to left; on a mismatch (or full match) the window is shifted to the right according to the standard Boyer–Moore shift rules. After such a shift, some positions in the new window have already been compared during the previous alignment, so their values relative to $x$ are known and the corresponding comparisons need not be repeated.

Define the "Boyer–Moore DFA for $x$" as the deterministic finite automaton over the input alphabet $\Sigma$ that simulates this enhanced search exactly: each state encodes the complete information accumulated by the algorithm so far (current alignment of $x$ against the text and the set of window positions whose contents, relative to $x$, are already known together with what is known about them), and on reading the next text character the automaton performs the rightmost not-yet-resolved comparison, applies all forced Boyer–Moore shifts and bookkeeping updates, and moves to the resulting state. Let $S(x)$ denote the number of states of this minimal automaton.

Determine $S(x)$ exactly as a function of the pattern $x$, or give matching (or near matching) upper and lower bounds on $S(x)$ in terms of $m = |x|$ and $|\Sigma|$.
artifact.status_search_result: The problem of determining the exact state complexity of a Boyer–Moore DFA was posed as an open question in stringology. Subsequent work (e.g., Blumer–Blumer–Ehrenfeucht–Haussler–Chen–Seiferas style automata theory, and specifically papers titled "On Boyer-Moore automata" in Algorithmica and "About the Size of Boyer-Moore Automata") has produced upper and lower bounds on the size of such automata and efficient construction algorithms, but a closed-form exact count $S(x)$ for arbitrary patterns does not appear to be established. The problem is therefore best described as partially solved (bounds known, exact formula not known in general).

status_evidence.title: On Boyer-Moore automata
status_evidence.snippet: The notion of Boyer-Moore automaton is formalized with efficient building algorithms, and bounds on the number of states are presented.
status_evidence.claim: Bounds on the number of states of Boyer-Moore automata have been established, and efficient construction algorithms exist.

status_evidence.title: About the Size of Boyer-Moore Automata
status_evidence.snippet: Lower bounds on the maximum number of states of Boyer-Moore automata are presented.
status_evidence.claim: Lower bounds on the maximum number of states of Boyer-Moore automata have been obtained, but an exact general formula has not been pinned down.
